# Dupe Detective

> Dupe Detective is a receipt scanner for iPhone and Mac. You scan a paper receipt and the app highlights any item that appears more than once, such as an item scanned twice at the register. Receipts are processed on the device and sync through the user's private iCloud database; the developers cannot access them.

- App Store: https://apps.apple.com/us/app/dupedetective-receipt-scanner/id6773174333
- Support: support@dupedetective.tech
- Privacy policy: https://chaffeesapps.github.io/dupedetective-privacy/

## Pages

- [Home](https://dupedetective.tech/): what the app does and how it works
- [FAQ](https://dupedetective.tech/faq): privacy, iCloud sync, deleting data, refunds

## Guides

- [Why was I charged twice? 5 common reasons](https://dupedetective.tech/blog/why-was-i-charged-twice): Most "double charges" are a temporary pending hold sitting next to the final charge, and the hold drops off on its own within a few days. A real duplicate happens when a payment is submitted twice, usually because a card reader froze, a cashier retried the card, or an online checkout was clicked or refreshed twice. If both charges have posted, contact the merchant first, then your card issuer.
- [Double charged? What to do next](https://dupedetective.tech/blog/double-charged-what-to-do): First make sure it's not a pending hold that will drop off on its own. Then ask the store to refund the duplicate, with your receipt in hand. If the store won't fix it, dispute the charge in your banking app or by calling the number on the back of your card, within 60 days of the statement.
- [Pending charge showing twice? How to tell if it's a real duplicate](https://dupedetective.tech/blog/pending-charge-showing-twice): If one of the two charges is still pending, it's usually an authorization hold, not a second payment. Debit card holds typically drop off within 1 to 5 business days. Credit card holds can last longer, and hotels and car rentals may hold funds for weeks. If both charges have posted, it's a real duplicate and you should contact the merchant.
- [Charged twice for an item at the grocery store? How to get a refund](https://dupedetective.tech/blog/charged-twice-grocery-store): Take your receipt to customer service and point out the item that was scanned twice. Most stores refund the extra charge on the spot. If you've already left, call or go back with the receipt. If the store won't fix it, you can dispute the overcharge with your card issuer.
- [How to dispute a double charge with your bank or card issuer](https://dupedetective.tech/blog/how-to-dispute-a-double-charge): Open your bank or card app, tap the duplicate charge, and choose "Dispute" or "Report a problem." Or call the number on the back of your card. Say you were charged twice for one purchase. Do it within 60 days of the statement that shows the charge.
- [Double charged on a debit card: how long until you get your money back?](https://dupedetective.tech/blog/double-charged-debit-card): If one charge is pending, it will usually drop off within 1 to 5 business days. If both charges posted, dispute it in your banking app or call the number on the back of your card right away. Under federal rules, the bank generally has 10 business days to investigate, or up to 45 days if it gives you a provisional credit within those first 10 business days.
- [How to check your receipt for errors in 30 seconds](https://dupedetective.tech/blog/how-to-check-receipt-for-errors): Before you leave the store, check five things on your receipt: the same item appearing twice, sale prices that didn't apply, coupons that are missing, weighed items with the wrong weight, and voided items that still show a charge. Then make sure the total matches your card slip.
- [How to spot a duplicate charge on a receipt](https://dupedetective.tech/blog/spot-duplicate-charges-on-receipts): Look for the same item and price on two lines, an item count higher than what's in your bags, and weighed produce entered twice. On your card statement, two posted charges for the same amount minutes apart usually mean the payment went through twice. A pending charge next to a posted one is usually just a hold.
